Who We Are

Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company that puts its members' financial goals within reach. With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually.
The Opportunity

We’re looking for a Senior DataOps Engineer to help operate, scale, and improve the data platforms that support Oportun’s analytics, engineering, and business teams. This role will focus on Databricks, AWS, data pipelines, databases, observability, automation, and production support.

You’ll be responsible for keeping critical data-platform services reliable, secure, performant, and cost-effective while partnering closely with Data Engineering, Analytics, Security, Cloud Infrastructure, Database, and application teams. Success in this role means improving platform reliability, reducing operational friction, strengthening automation, and helping teams resolve issues quickly and sustainably.

At Oportun, we move fast and we hold each other to a high bar. If you care about doing your best work while actually moving the needle for real people, you'll fit right in.

What You'll Do

Your day-to-day

• You’ll administer and support Databricks workspaces, cluster policies, compute configurations, jobs, workflows, libraries, service principals, permissions, and platform integrations.

• You’ll support Unity Catalog, including access governance, catalog and schema permissions, and secure data sharing.

• You’ll monitor and troubleshoot Delta Live Tables, Spark jobs, Delta Lake workloads, and data pipelines, including failures, performance issues, recovery, and data-quality concerns.

• You’ll maintain secure and reliable integrations between Databricks and AWS services, including S3, IAM, networking, VPC connectivity, and external data sources.

• You’ll support AWS infrastructure used by the data platform, including EC2, VPC, IAM, security groups, networking, patching, and operational access.

• You’ll support MariaDB/MySQL and MongoDB environments, including availability, monitoring, connectivity, backup coordination, performance troubleshooting, and recovery.

• You’ll build and maintain monitoring, dashboards, logs, metrics, and alerts across Databricks, pipelines, databases, infrastructure, and integrations.

• You’ll participate in on-call support and lead investigation, mitigation, recovery, communication, and root-cause analysis for production incidents.

• You’ll build and maintain infrastructure and automation using Terraform, Terraform Enterprise, Git, GitHub Actions, CI/CD pipelines, and scripting.

• You’ll automate repeatable operational activities such as provisioning, access configuration, monitoring deployment, recovery, and platform changes.

• You’ll manage secure access controls, secrets, certificates, TLS configuration, service accounts, and IAM roles across platform services.

• You’ll improve operational readiness through runbooks, recovery procedures, architecture diagrams, standards, escalation paths, and technical documentation.

• You’ll partner with engineering and infrastructure teams to improve capacity planning, platform performance, cost visibility, and resource optimization.

• You’ll look for practical ways to use AI and automation to improve troubleshooting, documentation, incident response, and operational efficiency.

Who You Are

The right fit looks like this

You’re a hands-on platform engineer who enjoys solving complex production problems and improving the systems behind critical data workloads. You think beyond the immediate issue, look for root causes, and build solutions that make the platform more reliable and easier to operate.

You’re comfortable working across cloud infrastructure, data platforms, databases, automation, and security. You communicate clearly during incidents, take ownership through resolution, and consistently look for ways to reduce repetitive work and improve operational maturity.

What You Bring

Skills & experience

Required

• Strong experience supporting production data platforms, cloud infrastructure, or DataOps environments.

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

Fraud & Safety Delivery (FSD) is at the heart of keeping Airbnb safe for the millions of hosts and guests who trust our platform every day. As part of Global Operations, FSD reviews and resolves potential fraud and safety cases across the full user lifecycle, with internal and partner specialists operating 24/7 across the globe.

You'll join Frontline Operations, the pillar that does that review and resolution work. Our specialists and the partner teams who deliver alongside us handle cases around the clock, and the leads, managers and analysts across the pillar make sure that work is fast, accurate and consistent wherever it runs.

You'll lead a team on Fraud & Safety Review within Frontline Operations, working day to day with Policy, Product and the partner sites that carry cases alongside your team.

 

The Difference You Will Make

You lead a team of Fraud & Safety Review specialists: you decide how their work is prioritised as volume, risk and resourcing move through the week, and you coach the judgement that makes their decisions consistent whoever handles the case.

The difference you make is a team that performs to a high standard all the time — not only when volume is manageable. That reliability is what the rest of FSD plans around.

Success looks like a team that consistently meets its quality, service-level and resolution-time targets, fewer repeat escalations because a change is applied the same way by everyone, and specialists who stay and grow because the path in front of them is clear.

 

A Typical Day

  • Lead and develop a team of Fraud & Safety Review specialists, holding the team accountable for quality, timeliness, and service goals while championing their growth and overall team engagement.
  • Adapt the team's plan and make the day-to-day decisions on case handling, escalation and coverage as volume, case mix or resourcing shifts. For example: rebalancing the queue and re-cutting coverage when a surge in account-takeover reports lands on a public holiday with half the team off.
  • Coach and develop your specialists through regular 1:1s and case reviews, manage performance against targets, and model the values and belonging behaviours that make the team people stay.
  • Use judgment and the operational data to resolve the technical, customer and operational problems your team raises, and recommend the process and tooling improvements the pattern points to.
  • Take process, tooling and workflow changes as an input from the broader fraud and safety strategy and land them with your team, and hand off the cases that need executive escalation or new precedent to the appropriate senior stakeholder.
  • Watch your team's operational metrics, report the trends and risks in your remit to leadership, and anticipate resourcing needs so you can raise a gap to your manager before it becomes a blocker.

 

Your Expertise

  • 8+ years in Fraud & Safety, Risk, Trust or related operations, including 4+ years leading or supervising a team in a high-volume, time-sensitive case-review environment.
  • Proven ability to hold a team of specialists to consistent quality, accuracy and productivity targets, using operational data to see where performance is moving and act on it.
  • Working knowledge of fraud and safety typologies, and how workflow, precedent and policy interact on escalated cases.
  • People leadership at the scope named above — led a team of specialists whose decisions carried real consequence, coaching a diverse group of talent and setting team priorities and performance targets.
  • Sound operational judgment when the answer is not clear — you assess the situation, decide with the information you have, and adapt the plan rather than waiting for direction.
  • Clear, direct communicator — able to make operational and case reasoning legible to your specialists, to your cross-functional partners, and to the leadership tracking your team's results.
  • Experience in a marketplace, travel or platform fraud and safety environment, or building SOPs, playbooks and enablement that scaled beyond one team, is a plus, not a requirement.

About Colonist

We're building the biggest digital board game platform on the internet. Players start 250k games every day. Last year: 60M games, 3,037 years of play. We're a fully remote, asynchronous team spread across multiple continents, focused on crafting extremely polished digital board games that people truly love.
About The Role
Most apps scale by splitting users apart. We can't. Players share one live game state. Every lag spike is felt mid-game. One viral video can 10x our traffic overnight. Your job: absorb 50k CCU without dropping a single game. 
You will own the infrastructure behind every game session: clusters, deploys, databases, the edge, and the path from merge to production. You will make our infra knowledge shared, so no system depends on one person.
What You'll Do

• 
Own the stack behind every game: game, matchmaking and lobby servers on Kubernetes

• 
Manage cluster and cloud resources as code in Terraform

• 
Scale servers up and down with live traffic. Pay for players, not idle machines

• 
Ship updates often, without kicking players out of live games

• 
Keep terabytes of game data and replays fast and cheap. PostgreSQL, Redis, NATS under real load

• 
Defend the edge from bots and attacks. Cloudflare, rate limiting, Turnstile, R2.

• 
Own observability across Sentry and New Relic. Consolidate monitoring and close the gaps

• 
Document everything: systems, decisions, runbooks, so infrastructure knowledge lives in the team

• 
Build self-service paths so other engineers use infrastructure confidently.

• 
When something breaks, thousands notice in seconds. Find the root cause. Make it never recur

Requirements

• 
You love hard technical problems. Scale, latency and cost excite you

• 
You have senior-level experience in DevOps

• 
You have run Kubernetes in production: rollouts, autoscaling, networking, load balancers, and debugging a bad deploy

• 
You run infra lean. You optimize before adding hardware

• 
You document as you go. Runbooks and decisions are natural outputs of your work.

• 
You are comfortable with Linux, Docker, and a CI system you did not build

• 
You have operated PostgreSQL and Redis under real traffic: slow queries, connection limits, and schema migrations without downtime

• 
You have run a message broker in production; we use NATS, but equivalent experience transfers

• 
You have put Cloudflare, or a similar edge, in front of a public service

• 
You can debug a live incident across app logs, metrics, the database, and the edge

• 
AI-forward mindset. We see AI fluency as a real multiplier

• 
Deeply independent. You learn a system from its code, configs and monitoring.

• 
Strong written communication. You explain complex systems clearly in async settings, to technical and non-technical audiences alike

• 
Collaborative by default. You share context proactively, help other engineers understand infrastructure, and never operate as a silo

Nice to Have

• 
Experience structuring documentation for AI consumption: machine-readable runbooks, structured architecture notes, agent-readable formats

• 
Experience building self-service infrastructure paths for other engineers: golden paths, templates, or internal tooling

• 
Security depth beyond the basics: threat modelling, access control, audit practices, governance guardrails

• 
You've run real-time or multiplayer systems where shared state matters.

• 
Previous experience as a solo or near-solo infrastructure engineer at a small company

Our Values at Colonist

We strongly adhere to these values in our team - if these resonate, then you'll love working here!
Dependability
We're self-driven players who deliver without needing supervision. When we commit to something, we make it happen.
Ownership
We take full responsibility and go beyond our roles to improve Colonist.
Clear Communication
In our remote environment, written communication is key. We're direct, structured, and always keep our team in the loop.
Efficient Execution
We move fast and focus on impact. Instead of getting stuck on perfect solutions, we find practical ways forward and get things done.
Continuous Learning
We're curious problem solvers who love a challenge. We constantly seek new ideas, embrace feedback, and aren't afraid to change our minds when we're wrong.
Why Colonist

We have hard problems, most engineers only read about: live shared state, viral spikes, lean scale
